subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should OpenClaw fix this by making health/status/stability strictly RPC-first with no-maintenance CLI fallback, by adding a shared-state single-writer gateway lease, or by doing both?
rationale: The source path confirms mutable CLI-side state DB access, but the durable fix changes the ownership boundary among Gateway RPC observability, doctor migrations, plugin-state diagnostics, and operator recovery.

options.title: RPC-first plus gateway lease
options.body: Status, health, and stability should ask the running gateway first, and any direct file access while the gateway owns the state DB should be read-only/no-maintenance unless an explicit repair lease is held.

options.title: RPC-first only
options.body: Remove the reported health/status/stability mutation path quickly, but leave broader non-gateway writers for a later ownership pass.

options.title: Forensics before implementation
options.body: Pause code changes until the reporter's corrupt DB bundle and a native OpenClaw SQLite harness confirm the exact bundled-runtime failure mode.

recommendation.title: RPC-first plus gateway lease
recommendation.body: Status, health, and stability should ask the running gateway first, and any direct file access while the gateway owns the state DB should be read-only/no-maintenance unless an explicit repair lease is held.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision cuts across the SQLite state-store architecture introduced in PR 78595 and the current gateway/CLI ownership boundary.
